utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, we've had the opportunity of reading the statements. I understand both of them are referred to in the application. We are satisfied that they come within the Rule. They are cumulative about events in Bratunac, about killings and also generally about killings and deportations -- not deportations, I mean detentions in Bosnia. They fit within the Rule and therefore, we will admit them. Plainly we take into account when it comes to cross-examination the fact that this is a 92 bis witness, and therefore, as a result the accused's time for cross-examination must take account of that and must not be diminished because the witness has given his evidence in that way. As I say, Mr. Nice, we've read the statements. We note that parts to be given live. We would encourage you not to spend too long, of course, on the live evidence since we've read the statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm grateful for that and I will indeed be succinct. The Court will notice a new face sitting beside me. Preparation of this witness was done, for the large part, by Ms. Bibles, with whom you are familiar and Mr. Pugliatti who sits next door to me. Ms. Bibles is away on Tribunal business, public Tribunal business elsewhere and in those circumstances I have the assistance of Mr. Pugliatti beside me. May the witness come in or arrangements be made for him to come in. Can we distribute if they haven't been distributed already exhibit files and have a look at those, perhaps if we have time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think we have them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Four tabs. So if the 92 bis package can be given one exhibit label.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, the next one.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Prosecutor's Exhibit 439.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That's the 92 bis package, is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And do you want a number for --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: A number for the exhibits themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that's Prosecutor's Exhibit 440, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: There's also a map or a couple of maps he'll be looking at. I'll deal with those separately. There is a summary that I will be, broadly speaking, following. That's not, of course, to become exhibited but if that could be or has been distributed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, it was distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. The witness take the declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If you'd like to take a seat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the duration of these proceedings, you will be known as Witness B-1070, 1070. Will you look, please, at this document which is tab 1 of Exhibit 450 and confirm by saying yes, if it is the case, that that is your proper name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: 440. Your Honour, if the witness could then please have a map which is going to form part of the map collection. It's a map that has been marked by him and will become Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecutor's Exhibit 336.B-1070.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The map before Your Honours has annotations to assist, figures 1 to 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm not sure I have the map. Where would it be?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Coming separately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Witness B-1070, does this map show at positions 1, 2, 3, and 4, 1, Bratunac; 2, Kasaba; 3, above Kasaba, Konjevci; and 4, lying on the road between Konjevci and Bratunac, a place where there is village or hamlet called Kravica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness B-1070, you may not have been informed of this and therefore I should do it, we're going to be taking your evidence in the short form that was discussed with you as a possibility yesterday. It's right that you made two statements which have been exhibited to the Court and read by the Judges, and I'm just going to read out a summary of your evidence so that you can sit back, and you needn't look at the map for the time being, sit back and just listen to the summary of your evidence that I'm going to read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, this witness worked in Nova Kasaba where the main Belgrade to Sarajevo road runs. He observed an increase in military traffic on that road in 1991 and in 1992 compared with the volume of military traffic in the previous 15 years with which he was directly familiar. He observed on one occasion a convoy that stopped and asked for directions to Kravica, point 4 on the map, which is a Serb village in the area. The Chamber will probably know this already. Bratunac itself a mixed community, but these outlying villages, Kravica, Serb villages. Separately, and late on the night of the 26th of December of 1991, the witness saw a van and car with Austrian licence plates in the neighbourhood, that is in his home neighbourhood, from which weapons were being distributed to neighbours who were Serbs. He saw Serb forces come into the town of Bratunac on the morning of the 17th of April, and together with members of the local territorial force, those forces assumed control of the town, there being no resistance offered. The Serb forces including Serb paramilitary forces. He was aware of one particular group identified as Arkan's men present and based in something called the Jasen cafe or restaurant which was across the road from the Bratunac mosque. In the next few days he observed JNA soldiers coming into the town, with one of whom he spoke in the Bratunac post office, that soldier advising him that the troops were from the Semberija Corps from Vojvodina, Srem, and from Banat in Serbia. About the time that members of the Semberija Corps appeared in Bratunac, special police arrived from Belgrade dressed in civilian clothes, stationing themselves at a school called Haca Mithat. Muslim men were arrested, interrogated and killed during this time and included in those were friends of this witness. His precise history is set out in his statements, he spending time substantially at home but then being arrested and interrogated by one of the Belgrade MUP officers. On the 10th of May, Your Honour, perhaps as the Court has read the material it's one detail worth drawing out without getting it from the witness is that the particularly horrifying details of his initial interrogation was that as he left the house, shots were fired, in fact into air but he was told that his family had been killed, his wife and children. He was then interrogated in the belief that he had lost his family. They'd been told that he'd been killed, but he was in due course released to find this was not the case, or each of them to find that it was not the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 10th of May, the witness and his family were forced from their home at gunpoint, taken to the stadium in Bratunac. Now, I think the Chamber will find at tab 4 an annotated aerial plan which perhaps we can place on the overhead projector. And if at any time the Chamber needs to see this part of the aerial view of Bratunac set in a larger aerial view photograph, that can be arranged, but using an A4 paper is always convenient. He was forced with his family at gunpoint to the Bratunac stadium shown on this photograph. There, members of the Bratunac Territorial Defence, the reconnaissance and sabotage unit as well as Serb paramilitaries were engaged in the process of ethnic cleansing that was to follow. The witness was in a position to recognise amongst these men some of the men he'd seen in the Arkan's unit when they first arrived in Bratunac. The stadium was surrounded by members of the regular police, reserve soldiers, and members of the Semberija Corps as well as the Semberija Corps's armoured personnel carriers, and there were more than 3.000 people, men, women, and children, gathered in the stadium. Muslims were told to hand in identification documents, money, gold, and valuables and threatened that anybody who declined to do so would be killed. Later, the detainees were ordered to walk towards the stadium exits where trucks and buses were parked. The population of that stadium being divided, women, children, boys under 15 and elderly men over 60 going one way, men of fighting age going the other. That group, of course, including this witness. The women, children, elderly and young were loaded into buses and trucks. The men were taken on foot in columns to the local gymnasium at the Vuk Karadzic school, marked as the Chamber can see on the photograph. That male group totalled some 700 to 750 people -- men, but number kept in the gymnasium increased over the next few days by about a further 300, bringing, therefore, the total population to about a thousand. Of that thousand, the witness's statements reveal in horrifying detail the majority were killed. Indeed, only about 401 or only 401 survived the next three days of killings to be transferred to Pale. The conditions inside the hangar were appalling, terrifying, and horrifying. While he was there, such was the enthusiasm of the captors for looting that he was forced three times to go back to his house for the purpose of locating jewellery and valuables, indeed on one occasion dug up the entire garden. It was obvious to the witness that the Belgrade MUP members were in a position of authority over other Serbs, and they were in a position to do exactly what they wanted. Included in the details he gives from within his -- in his statement of things that were done is an account of a Muslim holy man clearly target because he was a religious leader, forced to drink beer and other alcoholic drinks, to sing Chetnik songs and to raise his fingers in a Serb salute, thereafter being tortured for some 24 hours until he died. Another particularly distressing part of his account, which the Chamber will almost inevitably have found itself focusing on in one form or another, is of a man who was obliged by the captors to choose between which of his two sons present there with him should be shot. The man unable to make that decision, all three of them were shot in consequence. In due course, the witness and 400 others were transported to Pale where they were exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness B-1070, I've only got a few questions in addition to that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. summary to ask you about, but first of all, just one or two matters of detail which we can take from the exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can the witness see, please, Exhibit 440, tab 2 which is available of course in the original B/C/S version and an English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this document records?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: This document records a list of persons who were from the primary school called Vuk Karadzic taken to Pale.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May the witness now see tab 3 of Exhibit 440.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: This is the Bratunac mosque which was destroyed on the 11th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is this the mosque opposite which were stationed Arkan's men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That is the mosque opposite the restaurant called Jasen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I have one patch to show the witness. This is 349 -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's Prosecutor's Exhibit 349, tab 13.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you tell us about this patch? Where, if at all, did you recognise it in the course of your days of detention?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I didn't see this patch while I was in detention. However, I did see it on the 17th of April in front of the hotel called Fontana, and it was on the uniforms of four persons wearing black uniforms, in fact, who were providing security for the building when there was a meeting being held there between the representatives of the municipal authorities of the SDS and the SDA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Then just a few --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If the witness can read the letters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you read the letters for us, please? It's in Cyrillic and if you can read what it says, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: The Serbian Chetnik Movement, Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going back over the general account of your history that I've given, Witness B-1070, in addition to Arkan's men, what other paramilitary units by name were you able to recognise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: From their entry, the 17th of April, there were only two paramilitary formations in Bratunac, the Eagles and Arkan's men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. There's one incident that I want you to deal with in particular detail. The Chamber may have seen it in the statement, but I think it's important to give it. It's on page 14 of Exhibit 449, and it's paragraph's 36.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Paragraph -- yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, 439.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I explained to the Judges in summarising your evidence how you were taken to your house from time to time in order that those who had detained you could try and find more loot. Did you return from one of those occasions to the gymnasium where water and some food was being distributed but where there was a great noise made by the detained civilians so that Arkan's and Seselj's men started shooting over the heads of people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That was on the third day before we were exchanged. I had come back from my own house, and I found chaos there. Among the 400 people there were four or five bottles of water. People were very thirsty, exhausted, and it was very hot weather generally. They started trying to get at those four or five bottles of water. And from the hangar that was next to the gym belonging to the primary school Vuk Karadzic, there was a machine-gun nest there and they started shooting above our heads at the gym.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of that incident or perhaps after -- after it, did you go to the entrance door of the school? And it may help if we have tab 4 on the overhead projector again, please, tab 4 of 440. It's there now, thank you. Did you go to the door of the gymnasium?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: After my return, that is to say when I came back from my house, I was taken off by two policemen, and they introduced themselves as policemen belonging to the Belgrade MUP. They asked me to give them money and other valuables, and then they went on to ask me about a car, whose car it was because they didn't have the keys to open it. So when I went into the hall, one of my friends told me whose car it was, and I went back to catch up with the policemen to tell them who the car belonged to. However, in front of the hall at the entrance I came upon the ruling structures of the Bratunac municipality, that is to say the Serb leaders, Mr. Miroslav Deronjic, Simic, and all the rest of them who were standing there and talking to the drivers who were driving away the corpses of the Muslims that had been killed from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two bits of detail then. Can you just list, beyond the names you've already given, any members of the leadership that you saw there, and can you tell us what conversation, if any, you overheard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: They were mostly the local Serbs from Bratunac. I think Dragisa Loncarevic was there, then a gentleman who worked in the MUP. I think his surname was Tesic. And several other men whose names I used to know, but I really can't recall all those names right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Conversation between the local Serb leadership and the drivers of the bodies, taking the dead bodies -- the driver's of the lorry taking the dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes. They were there for some 20 or 15 seconds, and I heard the question being asked, "And where did you take them?" And then I had to go back so they wouldn't notice me, so that I wouldn't have to join those that were being driven away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think really that we've covered enough detail, because it's all in your statement save only for this point that you may be able to assist the Judges with. Your statements made it clear that you saw the most terrible killings going on and that you were in a position to see who the killers were; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Unfortunately, yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as we've heard just now, you also were in a position even to overhear the role of the leadership as well as the role of the incoming Serbs in all that was happening. Your account reveals that of the thousand people detained, 400 were allowed to leave the premises and were ultimately exchanged in Pale. How -- can you explain how it came about from your understanding that 400 of you were potential eyewitnesses to these terrible crimes were allowed to be exchanged, allowed to be exchanged as opposed to being killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: After the exchange, we heard an explanation that somewhere around Sarajevo a large number of Serbs had been captured and that we were the only forces that the Serbs had at their disposal to exchange them with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As your statement reveals, even in Pale, although you weren't personally, I think, beaten in the time of detention, you were beaten and subjected to indignity at the time of the exchange, were you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I think that is either incorrectly written or the statement was incorrectly interpreted. At Pale, on one occasion they beat me up really very badly. And during the exchange, they beat us at two locations. And as you could see on the videos the consequences of those beatings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My error entirely. It wasn't the translation. Yes, you were beaten up seriously the once and then you were also beaten up at the transfer itself. Thank you very much. Will you wait there? You'll be asked some further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, first of all, I should like to make an objection regarding the sudden shortenings. You decided today that this witness who was to testify live should suddenly become a witness on the basis of his written statement. Not only are we seeing a whole series of witnesses from a civil war from a neighbouring state, but you're even abbreviating their testimony on the very day when they are giving it. I think that such a farce needs no further comment, but I wish it to go on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... I will repeat that so it is heard. Such a comment is totally improper. It's not for you to comment on the proceedings particularly in that impertinent [Realtime transcript read in error "pertinent"] manner. If you want to be listened to, behave yourself. We've ruled on this. Now, you can cross-examine. We'll decide how long you have as depending on how it goes along. If you're really going to read out a series of alleged offences towards Serbs there's little point in doing it and we'll move on. If you have some serious cross-examination of this witness you can make it. Particularly if you challenge any of his evidence. You should challenge it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I challenge his entire testimony, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. The transcript should be corrected. What I said was the "impertinent manner" in which you had done so, not "the pertinent manner."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: The transcript is up to you. As for the statement, of course I challenge it, in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Impertinent is spelled I-m-p-e-r-t-i-n-e-n-t. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope you heard me, Mr. May, even though we are discussing here a war in a neighbouring state, I am endeavouring to collect facts relevant to these statements for the truth to be heard as to what happened. Cross-examined by Mr. Milosevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. 1070, you say that you lived in the municipality of Bratunac up until the 10th of May, 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then after that, you became a member of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I was mobilised to the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the difference in relation to my question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: There's no difference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. 1070, that you personally --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, I wish to draw your attention to the fact that I'm talking about the personal engagement of this witness, not about any Serbian witnesses that you have cautioned me not to read out because that is of no interest to you. I understand that that doesn't interest you. I'm talking about the personal participation of this witness and the personal acts committed by this witness himself, so it relates to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that you, on the 14th of December, 1992, you personally, Mr. 1070, carried out crimes in the villages of Sikiric, Bjelovac, Loznicka Rijeka, all of these being in Bratunac municipality? Is that true? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: That is the greatest nonsense I've heard so far, because I provided this Tribunal with documents to prove that in those days I was at a quite different location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can assume very well that you did provide documents. Do you know the names of the following persons who are also your compatriots, which means Muslims, and who were also under the command of Naser Oric and his assistant Zulfo Tursunovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Could I please look at those names?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will read them out. I can't give them to you to look at because I have them in my notes. Do you know, therefore, Alija Ibric, father's name Mujo, Hidan Salihovic, Besim Salihovic, Reso --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's enough. Now, let the witness answer one by one. It will be much easier.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know those names. As for my name, you will see that it doesn't contain the name of any parent, nor the date of birth, nor the place of birth. Therefore, in those days, I was a member of the 2nd Corps of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I was stationed in Kladanj, and as proof, I have brought my military booklet with the stamp of the unit of which I was a member.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't doubt at all that you have documents to prove whatever you will, but please, since you're a protected witness, I can't ask you questions about your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you then tell me the name of that village?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think we'll going into private session for these matters.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You said you didn't know these names I read out, and do you know Dzemail Kamenica, Ramiz Kamenica, Munib, Esmo Kiveric, Midhat Salihovic, Adil Salihovic, Ekrem --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Break there. Witness B-1070, were you able to get -- were you able to get those names and do you know any of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am really sorry, but in our part of the world, there are many people with the same first and last names. To be able to say whether I know any one of them, I would have to know the father's name, date of birth, and the like. I think I don't know these names and that some surnames are not at all from Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know Mirsad Malagic and Mujo Malagic for instance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: That is a very common surname in Bratunac municipality, and in three or four local communities, there are people with those names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Since you participated in these crimes committed against Serbs in the villages of Sikirica, Bjelovac, and Loznicka Rijeka, do you know how many Serbs were killed and what their names were?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You've been told this. It's no point putting something to a witness which he's denied and it's particularly improper pretending he's accepted it, which you appear to be doing, and he hasn't. But the witness can be asked the latter part of it -- just a moment. It's alleged that you have killed Serbs. Now, Witness B-1070, you should have the chance of dealing with that. Have you killed any, and if so, what were the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I answer with full responsibility that I didn't kill a single Serb. I can say with full responsibility that I am not the person that the accused believes I am, and I think to call someone a war criminal without any proof, without knowing the full name and other particulars is impermissible. I do not consider the accused to be a war criminal until the court proves that he is a war criminal. And what he is alleging against me is extremely insulting for me, and I think it could cause problems for my family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness B-1070, do not be insulted. The accused is entitled to put allegations, which is all they are, which he says he has, to you. It is your answers which are the evidence, not what he says. What he says is not evidence at all. Your answers are the evidence, and you are entitled to deal with it and you have dealt with these allegations, and they're no more than that. And as you've explained, it's quite possible he's got the wrong man.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, you said that I was assuming that he had agreed to my allegation that he was involved in killings. I'm not pretending at all. I'm just stating that he did participate. I heard very well that he said that he didn't, which is of no surprise to me, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: But if the witness denies that, then you can't put it again as though it were a fact. That's the point. But let's go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. 1070, did you take part in the killing of 21 Serbs in the village of Sikiric in Bratunac municipality?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He has, first of all, denied that he killed any Serbs. So there's no point putting that all over again. Secondly, he's denied being involved in any crimes in Sikiric. So there's no point putting that all over again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on the 16th of May, I was exchanged at Visoko. In mid-August, I came to the Tuzla canton, and I was still recovering from the injuries sustained in the camps. After the 16th of May, I did not go back to Republika Srpska again until the end of the war. Therefore, I wasn't present in those areas at all at the time the accused claims those crimes occurred. So please let my name not be connected with something I have nothing to do with.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let's then move on to something that you are connected with. You say that you gave a statement to the authorities in Bosnia in July 1992. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When those events were fresh in your memory. And a lot of time has gone by since, and it is difficult for you to recollect all the names.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: At this point in time, I must be allowed to forget a name or two or be mistaken about a date, but the events have been so deeply imprinted in my memory that they cannot be forgotten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You still do remember that before the conflicts broke out that day-to-day life in the municipality was normal, that people got on well regardless of whether they were Serbs or Muslims. And you speak about that on page 2 of your statement, unless that is somebody else's statement. Is that your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes, we did get on, and there were no problems between us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that same paragraph that I referred to a moment ago, you say that it was like that right until the beginning of the war in Croatia in 1991 when, as you say, you noticed changes among your Serb friends, because they were advocating more stronger feelings about Serbian nationalism.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes, because a large number of Serbs from Bratunac would regularly attend your rallies that you were holding all over Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, do you remember the 1st of September, 1990, when the founding assembly was held of the Party of Democratic Action? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't even remember the founding assembly meeting of the SDA that was held in a rather heated, militant atmosphere? You don't remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Politics was absolutely of no interest to me. I was satisfied to be able to live and have a decent life, and as I had no plans of making a political career, I had no interest in them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I see that you were interested in rallies in Serbia, yet you were not interested in a rally in your own town. That doesn't seem to be very logical, does it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Well, you asked me a question as to when the change in the feelings of Serbs could be felt towards Muslims and other peoples.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that this was linked to the war in Croatia. What did the Muslims have to do with the war in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: In my view, none. However, a large number of soldiers of the Yugoslav People's Army, regular soldiers of the Yugoslav People's Army were at the front in Croatia. Among them, Muslims as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Muslims were there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the time has come when it would be helpful for the witness to have the statement before you particularly if the accused is going to be putting propositions derived from the statement. It will also help all of us if the accused identifies the relevant statement by the handwritten number in the margin, because I think the page numbers of the B/C/S and English versions may not coincide and in any event the whole purpose of having numbered paragraphs is to enable swift identification of the relevant part of any statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. The witness can have the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. 1070. Do you remember over a thousand Muslims in Bratunac who demonstrated in the streets because, as you say, you don't remember the founding assembly session of the SDA. Do you remember those demonstrations? They were rather militant. Do you remember threats made to the Serbs and cries that "Bosnia belongs to Muslims and Serbia belongs Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to Serbs, that Serbs should go to Serbia"? Do you remember those events in Bratunac municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I really don't remember these events. You'd have to refresh my memory, what events are you talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the demonstrations in Bratunac in 1990. I'm talking about these events. You said it was Serbs who started feeling animosity towards the Muslims, and I have information here exactly to the opposite.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: You had information also that I was a war criminal, and I don't even remember there were any demonstrations in 1990.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't remember any demonstrations in Bratunac. Let's take this off the agenda.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: You'll have to refresh my memory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember Muslim demonstrations in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: What demonstrations?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember any demonstrations at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I remember two Muslim protest rallies. The first one was when the army had come to take away military records, and the second was after the murder and -- murder of two Muslims and wounding of one Muslim, but I think it was in 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you answer me, is it true that as early as in mid-1991, 1991, I'm not talking about 1992 yet, the leadership of the Party of Democratic Action organised illegal procurement of weapons and establishment of military units? Is that true or not? Just tell me yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: You'd have to ask the people from the SDA, because I am not a member. And I was never offered a barrel or ammunition, nor did anyone inform me that any such activities were being carried out on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know that in mid-1991 Reza Muhic [phoen] set up his own unit consisting of 50 men, precisely in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know nothing about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything at all about the events which made Serbs, as a minority in Bratunac, fear all the more for their safety, and as early as in the beginning of 1991, they started hiding their children at the houses of their relatives from Bratunac. Do you know why they started feeling insecure and unsafe?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's deal with this in two sections. What is alleged is the Serbs were in a minority in Bratunac. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only during the census was it that I learned that the Serbs were a minority. In every other way, they were equal. There was no way you could tell that they were a minority in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Was there any indication in 1991 in the beginning that they, the Serbs, were in fear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I lived in the town of Bratunac where the population is 50/50. Very openly and under full responsibility I assert that from the town of Bratunac, not a single Serb left under duress or pressure, nor did anyone hide their children away all the way until April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what I was saying is not correct, that they hid their children away from Bratunac due to those threats, demonstrations, pressure exerted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He just said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you remember that it was precisely these extremists of the SDA who used every cultural sports event or any large gathering of people to promote Islamic and Ustasha symbols and iconography and to make threats to Serbs in Bratunac? Do you remember anything of the atmosphere that was being created then and who did it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I was a member of the management of the football club in Bratunac which consisted of both Muslims and Serbs. In that football club, 60 per cent of players were Serbs. Perhaps only 40 per cent were Muslims. And the club successfully continued until the beginning of 1992. And I claim under full responsibility that at all football matches, not a single national flag was waved. Not a single national slogan was cried out. And as for local village clubs in villages which were ethnically pure, either Serb or Muslim, I don't know what happened. I was not interested in those villages at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you remember at least the -- the event in the primary school in Kravica? For decades, children from the surrounding villages were schooled there regardless of whether they were Serbs or Muslims. You must remember that Muslims, in order not to mix with Serb children, organised an ethnically pure primary school in Konjevic Polje and named it Babo Hamza. Religious teaching was introduced there and exclusively Muslims were schooled.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Konjevic Polje is 20 kilometres away from Bratunac. I have absolutely no connection, no links to that village, and I don't know why you're asking me questions about matters like this because I told you I didn't belong to any political party. I wasn't interested in politics. Seventy per cent of all my friends were Serbs, and if anything was going on, believe me, I would not be entrusted with any responsibility because the people I socialised with were mostly Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that those Serbs, friends of yours, committed any crimes against Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: No. Friends remain friends, and they are still my friends today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you don't want to say this in open session, tell me in closed session. Do you still live in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: No. My property has not yet been restored to me, the property I have in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Do you remember any events from 1992 that took place in Bratunac, the shattering of windows there, burglaries in kiosks --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the year 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember any intimidation of Serbs to make them leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: The shattering of windows -- the burglaries in kiosks, I do remember. Because they took place even before these events and Kiosks and shops are always broken in and everybody knows why.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is really witty, and it's true I suppose as well. But I'm talking about violence as means of intimidation. You don't remember any of that, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: In the town where I lived, the population was half/half, Muslim and Serb, and I claim under full responsibility that until April 1992, in that area there were no incidents whatsoever, not on ethnic or religious grounds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what it makes it so insane that you began killing each other in such an ethnically mixed community?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: The funny thing is that's not the way I remember it. I don't remember that we were killing each other. I remember that we were being killed. I don't remember a figure of 1.000 killed Serbs. I only remember 1.000 Muslims who were killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that in Bratunac municipality there was more than one terrible massacre of Serbs and many Serb villages were razed to the ground? A lot of population who was unable to escape was killed. You know nothing about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Give me a single example before the 10th of May of Muslims committing a single crime in Bratunac against the Serb population. After the 10th of May, I was expelled from my own hometown, from my own town. I went elsewhere, and what went on in Bratunac, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Help us with this, Mr. Milosevic, if you would. When is it alleged that the killings of these Serbs took place?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, I will answer your questions when it's my turn to testify, and you cannot ask me questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. But it would help us, you see -- it would help us in trying to understand the position if we knew when it was you said -- you allege that these killings took place. Otherwise, we will assume that they took place after the takeover of Bratunac in April. That seems to be what happened. If you say otherwise, you should tell the witness. He must have a chance to answer it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll put my questions to the witness the way I see fit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. I'm going to -- just a moment. You can wait. Help us with this: You've said that relations were good in Bratunac. It may help us get a picture. And most of your friends were Serbs, and the football club went on playing, and then in April, these terrible things happened which the accused has so far not challenged. Three hundred -- 600 people killed in the gymnasium. Was it your impression that this was the local Serbs who were responsible for what happened or was it people who came in from outside, from Serbia and the rest? What -- who -- you were there at the time. Who did you think was doing all this, or can you not really say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for the killings, the killings were committed by people who had come from outside. As for orders, orders were issued by the top leadership of the SDS. And as to who provided lists of people, because nobody was killed casually or randomly. Nobody was just randomly stopped in the street. Everybody was arrested and killed according to lists. I suppose the lists were provided by local Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's clear up at least this issue, Mr. 1070. I noted that you said in this abbreviated testimony of yours, in the few words that you said viva voce, from the time they entered on the 17th of April, there were two paramilitary units. That's the way you put it, two paramilitary formations. My question is: Did you at any point during these events see any presence of the Yugoslav People's Army or any police unit from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes, during the ethnic cleansing of village, the forces that accompanied the Territorial Defence were APCs and tanks of the JNA. And as for the police, the Belgrade MUP, it was them who took me into custody. They introduced themselves. And the people who guarded me before the inspector came to interrogate me, the inspector was said to belong to the Belgrade MUP. And they took me three times to my house to show them where the money or gold jewellery or God knows what was allegedly hidden.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. 1070, is it clear to you that people from the Belgrade police force would never go to do a thing like that even as near as Loznica in Serbia? It would be done by the police from Loznica or Sabac or any other place. Do you really believe that people from the Belgrade police came from Bratunac to dig up your gold?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Unfortunately, we live in such times that you start believing everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in principle, that might be true, but how many were those people who introduced themselves as members of the Belgrade police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Three of them said they were from the Belgrade police. The first one who questioned me that day was nicknamed Bane. There were another two Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. who said they were from the Belgrade police who took me home, and it was 11 of them who came to arrest me the first day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So three of them said they were from the Belgrade police force.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they identify themselves? Did they show their IDs which they were supposed to do when carrying out official actions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, it was the kind of time when nobody introduced themselves. It was a time when people were mistreated without trial, without evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. 1070, certainly it was the worst possible time. In civil war, everybody kills everybody. But I'm asking you now, kindly please set that aside. On what basis did you say that those three men who came to ask you to dig up some sort of money were from the Belgrade police, unless it was because they just said so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were really from the Belgrade police. However, I was born on the bank of the Drina River three kilometres away from the border with Serbia, and I know very well and claim with full responsibility that these people were from Serbia, because Bosnian Serbs, however hard they tried to speak the Serbian Serbian language, they never manage. Whether they were really members of the Belgrade police or not, I cannot know. They said they were, and the guards said they were. Why they said so, you should ask them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Now, in view of the fact that the person that was -- as somebody who was interested in the events, have you read the book by Besim Ibisevic, the president of the Municipal Assembly of Srebrenica, for example? That might have interested you. About the events that took place in your parts. Have you read his book?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I'm really sorry to have to say that I have not read a single book linked to that area and describing those events. Those books were written by people who fled before the conflict actually broke out, and they left the people to fend for themselves. I belong to the ordinary man who had to pay dearly for the events that took place. People leaving Bratunac on the 15th and 16th of April were quite different. So I'm not interested in books of that kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can well understand that. All I asked you is whether you had perhaps read the book so I can ask you some questions relating to the book, but as you have not I'm not going to ask those questions. And I do believe you when you say that you have not read the book. Now, tell me this, please, that they fled three days before the conflict broke out, your leadership in fact your leaders, I can well believe that. I really do believe you when you say that. In your statement, you mention that of the military facilities that existed, there was only a warehouse, a depot in the town of Bratunac. A moment ago, you also said that in the region in which these events came to pass that you saw some JNA units. Could you please now tell me quite precisely whether you did actually see any JNA members kill a single Muslim or, rather, any human being at all that you are testifying about in your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: The JNA units took part or, rather, assisted in the ethnic cleansing of Muslim villages. And I can say with full responsibility that I did not actually see a single JNA member kill anybody, any Muslim, because I didn't live in those villages. I wasn't there in the villages that were cleansed and burnt down where the people had been killed. All I can say is that in my particular village or, rather, my district, the district I was expelled from, nobody was killed until the arrival at the stadium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that the JNA precisely during that period of time had only one role to play and that was to quell the situation and to make it impossible for international -- for inter-ethnic conflicts to break out in its area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, the witness can only answer as to what he saw and heard. Generalised questions like that are of no assistance and cannot be answered by him. He says the JNA were there. Now, you can ask him about that, of course, as you have done about the individuals, but he said tanks and APCs were involved in the ethnic cleansing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, he said that he didn't see a single soldier, JNA soldier, kill a single Muslim. That is also what he said. Of course, you don't wish to hear that portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I'm asking you now, wasn't it perhaps -- did he not perhaps possess some information which would help us ascertain that the JNA was in fact endeavouring to stop the conflicts and clashes and to calm the situation, to calm the inter-ethnic conflicts or not? Perhaps he has information of that kind?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Wait a moment. That is a concrete question, and he can answer it. Did it appear to you or have you any information that the JNA was trying to stop the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, sir, in the period from the 10th to the 13th or, rather, the evening of the 13th of May when the largest massacres took place and when hundreds of people were killed in the Vuk Karadzic Primary School, the JNA was present. Why didn't it protect us? Why didn't it expel those paramilitary formations and protect the people in the gym who were being killed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: When you say it was present, would you clarify that? Where was the JNA when you were in the gym?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were in Bratunac. They had APCs. Their APCs continued to be parked in front of the Fontana Hotel. I know that one APC had broken down and that they took a mechanic over to try and repair it, but they never returned. And when they went to Pale -- when we were taken to Pale, two APCs escorted us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a second, Mr. Milosevic. I want to ask the witness in what numbers were the JNA present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't give you a number. I can't say exactly, but I would say there were one or two companies, for example, the strength of one or two companies. I know that there were transport APCs, and tanks and some infantry. They were put up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: The JNA entered Bratunac, I think, around the 20th of April or maybe the 21st of April, after the takeover of Bratunac by the Serb paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Was the JNA there in passing? Was it on its way from somewhere and going in the direction of somewhere else or had it arrived to carry out an assignment, a particular assignment in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I really can't say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when it appeared, that particular unit, the unit you talked about, and it will be easy for us to establish what was going on there, but on that occasion was anybody killed when they turned up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: After the JNA entered, the unit left. But two days later, it returned, and that's when the killings started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who returned? Who came back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: The unit, the paramilitary unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ah. So you're talking about a paramilitary unit, are you, not the JNA. Let's clear this point up. The JNA arrived in Bratunac and the paramilitary unit left Bratunac. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then the JNA left Bratunac and the paramilitary unit returned to Bratunac, is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: No. The JNA stand -- the JNA stood on in Bratunac and the paramilitary unit returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what stayed on in Bratunac except this broken down APC?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Well, not this broken down APC, the other transporters were there. The APCs that had taken place in the cleansing -- taken part in the cleansing in Bratunac throughout the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, these APCs, the one that escorted you to Pale, for example, those vehicles, what date was this? When did they escort you to Bratunac, these two APCs? What date was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I think it was the 14th of May. The 13th or 14th, in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, these APCs did they belong to the Republika Srpska or to the JNA, the ones that escorted you up to Pale?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Well, as far as I'm concerned, I think they belonged to the JNA. They had the five-pointed star as their emblem, and they were wearing olive green uniforms, and I considered them to be the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the people who were transported to Pale? Were they supposed to be protected? Were they being in fact protected?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: From whom?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anybody. How many of you were there? You say there were several hundred? That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes, 400 in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Four hundred. And the object of you being transformed was to be exchanged ultimately; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I assume so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I assume they were going to exchange you alive; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I assume by the same token that somebody was there to protect you if they wanted to exchange you alive.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Well, where were the APCs and units from the 10th to the 13th of May then?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I can't know that. I can't say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Why didn't they protect us when they ought to have done? Why didn't they expel those criminals, if I can call them that, who killed the innocent people in the halls, sports hall? Where were they then? And they were stationed behind the Fontana Hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. 1070, the people who killed innocent persons in the hall were certainly criminals, and I have no reason to say otherwise or enter into polemics with you about that. All I want to establish is whether that was done by the JNA. You said that you did not see a single JNA soldier kill anybody at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't in the field. I wasn't there when the ethnic cleansing of those villages took place, so I can't say something I don't know about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's why you can't claim that the JNA took part in any ethnic cleansing either; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This is all a matter of argument and comment. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then tell me this: You mentioned that of the military facilities there was only a warehouse or a depot in Bratunac and this is on page 3, paragraph 1 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes. And the warehouse was in the old tobacco company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You probably know that better than me. I'm reading your statement, so that's why I'm asking you. Now, is it also correct that in 1991, as far an a back as 1991, and I assume you'll know this, that the weaponry of the Territorial Defence which all the companies had, and factories too, was stolen? All those arms were stolen and transported to Muslim villages in the surrounding areas of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: No. That is not correct. The weapons from the warehouse of the Territorial Defence in Bratunac were taken away by the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This president of the municipality in his book says they even stole a cannon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Which mayor of mine, president of the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Ibisevic man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Was he not the mayor of Srebrenica and perhaps these warehouses and depots belong to Srebrenica and not Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My questions are about Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Well this, Besim Ibisevic probably didn't write a thing about the Bratunac municipality but Just about the depots of the Srebrenica municipality. As far as the warehouses in Bratunac are concerned, it was the army who took away the weapons. And you can check that out very easily. That would be no problem for you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that Serb nationalism was present, could be felt in some way. I'm reading from your statement, page 3, paragraph 3. "I knew that there were strong feelings of Serbian nationalism." But you say, "As far as I know, it was not directed against the Muslims." That means that there were no bad feelings or relationships between the Muslims and Serbs. Wasn't that how it was? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right then. Now, what caused, as far as I remember the elections were held, power was divided up among the main political parties, the SDA and SDS being the principal ones. That's right, isn't it, at least in those parts, in that area? The HDZ wasn't present there because there were very few Croats living in the area. So let me ask you this: The deterioration of all these relationships, mutual doubts, suspicions, fanning the flames of the conflict in fact was triggered by political events and the decisions made to -- for Bosnia and Herzegovina to secede from Yugoslavia. Wasn't that how the civil war in Bosnia began in fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Well, I really don't know how to answer that question. I'm not a politician. Politics is not something I know about. All I did happen to notice was that the Serbs' relationships towards the Muslims began to change in 1992 except for one killing that took place or rather two killings that took place between Konjevic Polje and Kravica. Otherwise, there were no other problems in the municipality. Or at least I didn't notice them because I lived in that kind of environment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you think that Bosnia had to separate, secede from Yugoslavia at all or was it normal to your mind that Bosnia was a part of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's not a politician. You asks all the witnesses these questions. Most of them have no idea at all. You can address us about it in due course and you can talk about the politics in due course. We will adjourn now. Half past ten. Witness B-1070, could you please be back in 20 minutes. During that time and during the time you're giving your evidence, don't speak to anybody else about it until it's over and that does include the members of the Prosecution team. We will adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We've considered the time you should have for this witness. We consider it on the basis that he is a live witness and therefore we don't consider it on the basis of the half hour or so which the Prosecution took. We notice that the estimate, it's only an estimate, was one of three hours, but we think that that is probably about right in this case and that they would have taken in chief had he given evidence live about an hour and a half, and accordingly, you should have an hour and a half yourself, which on my mathematics would give you an additional 40 minutes if you require it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we agreed that up until the end of 1991, according to your own statement, there were -- there was no hostility of the Serbs towards Muslims, that things started deteriorating rapidly in the first quarter, shall we say, of 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes. That is what I claim, because really in the part of town in which I lived, up until then there had been no hostilities between the two groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Since you say that you were not involved in politics, that you did not follow political developments, you simply felt that things had got worse at that time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wish to draw your attention, gentlemen, that that was the period of time when Cutileiro's plan fell through and when the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina was proclaimed on the basis of that illegal referendum, et cetera, et cetera. So this witness, who was not involved in politics, can serve very well to highlight the real reasons. Tell me, Witness, please, before these events of the 17th of April, do you know that in the village of Hranca, which is in the immediate vicinity, an ambush was set for a column of cadets withdrawing from Rajlovac and passing along that road and that they were fired upon in this ambush and that a large number of drivers and cadets were the target of that ambush and that the consequences were very serious? Do you remember that? This is an event which I assume could not have occurred without you noticing it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I think that you are misinformed and that didn't happen at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, I see. It didn't happen at all. Very well. And I have information here that precisely after that particular event, an armoured motorised company of the JNA came from Sehovici, a company that was stationed in Sehovici. They came with the task of disarming both Serbs and Muslims. They looked for the organisers of the ambush and demanded a surrender of weapons. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: No, because it didn't happen. That didn't happen, and I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Since you're testifying to the effect that several hundred people were killed in the events that occurred around that time, that only 400 of you were sent for an exchange and the rest were killed according to you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: In my estimate, and that is my alone, no one else's, that in the events in the period between the 10th and 14th or 15th of May, in the gym alone and around it, about 600 to 700 men were killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Because I really have no information about that. Do you know where this enormous number of people were buried?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: You would have to ask that of the Serbian authorities in Bratunac. I would also like those bodies to be found and to be given a dignified burial, because among them there are many of my relatives and hundreds of my friends and acquaintances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're claiming that they were killed, but you don't know where they were buried and it is not known where they were buried. Very well. As according to my information this didn't occur, you were all transported to Sarajevo and exchanged. Then according to your assessment, what was the criteria on the basis of which 400 of you were selected for the exchange and the rest killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: The 400 of us were not selected on the basis of criteria to be exchanged. In my judgement during the killing an order must have come from above to stop the killing and to allow the men to live to be exchanged. Otherwise, had it not been for that, they would have ended up like the men from Zvornik, Visegrad, and many other places where not a single surviving witness remains.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, did you personally see those killings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, it is very hard for me even to remember and think of those events. Unfortunately, I saw hundreds of them being killed. Tens in the hall of the elementary school. I saw eyes popping out from shots at the back of the head. I saw brains splattered. And we were asked to wipe them away with our T-shirts and to carry them. I saw bodies in front of the hall of men from Srebrenica who were executed on the first night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw all this with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes, I did. And not just I but 400 live witnesses who will also confirm this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Since you eyewitnessed all this, who did it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: It was done by a certain group of five men who executed all the killings that I saw in the hall of the Vuk Karadzic elementary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was that group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: They called each other by nicknames. One was Bane, another Makedonac, another Dragan, and I don't remember the names of the other two, or rather their nicknames.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these five men killed all those other men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes, those five men killed the men in the hall. Now, who was doing the killing outside, I really don't know, but these five men killed all those men that I saw being killed in the hall. They were the ones who did the torturing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, among the local leadership, who did you see while you were there in detention and when you were being taken away? Did you see any of the municipal leaders? Did you see any officials, Serbs, Muslims, or any one of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: In the -- Mr. Deronjic sent us from the stadium to the gym. In front of the gym I saw Mr. Deronjic, Mr. Simic, and some other local Serbs. I didn't see any of the Muslims because the authorities were Serb at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was Deronjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I think he was the president of the SDS in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see he was president of the party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was president of the municipality at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I think it was -- in the period prior to the 17th of April, the president of the municipality was a Muslim. But they left like the others. He left like the others. Now, who was president just then, I really don't know, because the elected official authorities had already left Bratunac. All that remain was the bare-handed population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one matter. Since you explained that you did not take part in any of these attacks or killings that I referred to but you were a member of the 2nd Corps, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From when were you a member of the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: From the 3rd of March, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. The 3rd of March, 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did the 2nd Corps cover, what area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: The Tuzla region area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does Srebrenica, Bratunac, and all these places come under that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: You know that those areas were cut off and that units of the 2nd Corps couldn't go there. They held positions around Tuzla, Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did the units in Srebrenica belong to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 3, paragraph 3 of your statement, you say that the situation changed, that you noticed at the entrance to your settlement certain checkpoints, and at those checkpoints were there any reserve policemen, both Serbs and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Let me find it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 3, paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I can't find that on page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Which statement is the accused referring to, the first or the second statement? And if he would give a page or paragraph number if he's using the handwritten paragraph numbers, I'll find the corresponding paragraph in the B/C/S version for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that this reserve police force consisted of both Serbs Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and Muslims at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I don't remember saying in any statement that there were checkpoints. The only checkpoint that I remember manned by reserve policemen was the checkpoint at Kravica. As for the reserve police force in those days, there were both Muslims and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We've got the passage now. In the English, it's on page 3, and it is paragraph 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: ICTY statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It's the ICTY statement and paragraph 11 of the ICTY statement can be found by the witness on a page perhaps the usher would help him, that has registry number 02132888 on the top right-hand corner there are two numbers printed on mine but it is the large figure 888. And it is, I think, the middle paragraph beginning with the word "Pamtim da". I think.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. No microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Microphone. Yes. You've got that, have you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I've found it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness finish.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I referred to a checkpoint, this applies to a particular date. It was that evening or that morning on the Konjevic Polje to Bratunac road. There was an ambush in which two Muslims were killed and one was wounded. And as I went to work every morning along that road, that day I couldn't pass. I had to make a detour, because that morning at the entrances to all the villages between Bratunac and Konjevic Polje there were barricades.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But you say already towards the end of the next paragraph that was the reason for the Minister of police Avdo Hebib from Sarajevo to visit the area. From this time onwards, checkpoints increased along with an increase in tension. Is that right? That is what you say at the end of that same paragraph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes. There was a permanent checkpoint at Kravica, and it was manned by the reserve police force, and it is true that not only did Avdo Hebib come to Bratunac, but I think Mr. Zepin, Mr. Ganic, and others came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you about that. This is September 1991, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I assume that was the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did on that occasion members of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Nikola Koljevic and Ejub Ganic come together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes. They even held a joint speech at the stadium which was attended I think by 5.000, both Serbs and Muslims, who greeted with applause this speech and this calming of tensions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, on that occasion in Bratunac, Kajici, Kravica, on the 4th of September, 1991, when Vitomir Zepin, Deputy Minister of the Interior and Avdo Hebib and Enver Saric, the chief of the security service from Tuzla, did they all come just before Ganic and Koljevic? So the event attracted a great deal of attention, and obviously efforts were made to calm the situation down.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: As I said, I can't remember the exact date, but I do know that these officials came and that efforts were made to appease the situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
