utterances.text: Very well. Were you aware of the barricades that were put up then to the approaches to Bratunac at villages of Glogova, Hranca, and Pervani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of barricades being put up to the entrance to each village in Bratunac municipality between Konjevic Polje and Bratunac. So not only Muslim villages but also Serbian villages, Derepuca [phoen], Kra -- Kajici, Kravica, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The barricades I'm mentioning in Glogova, Hranca and Pervani, were they Muslim barricades?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true in those localities vehicles of public transport were stopped and passengers, Serbs, mistreated and thrown out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: On that day?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I'm talking about a practice at those checkpoints that you yourself said were put up by Muslims.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I'm answering you whether you mean on that day, because the barricades were there for only one day. Until the police from Tuzla arrived, the road was closed and transport went along Bratunac-Polom-Zvornik, so round about that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true that the commander of the Pervani barricade was Mehmedalija Selimovic, who is well known because he boasted about that had attended training in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I'm telling you no one could pass any further than the first barricade. Traffic was stopped. I can answer your question because I passed through those barricades and I saw the people manning them. I think they were all removed about 2.00, 3.00, and I really don't know who was in charge of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. 1070. I believe you if you say you don't know. You really don't know. But is it true that people were intimidated then and that they started moving out? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I didn't notice that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You say on page 3, it's easy for you to find because it's open in front of you, you say something about an incident where in the vicinity of the municipal building you noticed about 20 soldiers who were firing into the air to intimidate people. You said those were conscripts under the command of a man called Redjo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Redjo is also a Muslim, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes. He was a JNA officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct. JNA officer. And he had come to collect military records.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was in keeping with the decision of the federal government, that the army should take over military records. You know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Really, Mr. Milosevic. I don't know anything about those decisions, and I had absolutely no interest in them, whichever government had taken them. I don't know in keeping with what that was done, but I know that the people were against it and didn't allow the documentation to be taken over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anyway, an incident happened then because activists at the SDA gathered civilians and didn't allow the army to come in, and those soldiers were under the command of an officer who was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was not an inter-ethnic clash, was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say they had come to take the names of conscripts so that they could send them call-up papers for the war. Do you know that the names were needed so that they could be called up into the war? How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: That's my opinion, and that is shared by many others. I heard rumours about that from the police. It doesn't mean that I can't be mistaken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, nobody is immune to mistakes, but we've just established that 20 soldiers who had come to take over the records were under the command of a Muslim. They had all come to collect military records in order to send call-up papers for the war. What war are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: The war in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people were organised on that occasion to prevent this unit commanded by Redjo from taking over the military records?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I really don't know whether it was organised or not, because I had arrived towards the end. Until 3.00 or thereabouts, I worked, and when I arrived in Bratunac around 4.00, it was already ending. I don't know how many people there were. Perhaps about a thousand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I have information that the number of people gathered was between 2.000 and 4.000?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any case, you can't confirm this piece of information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I cannot confirm what?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say there were several hundred people.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: It's a big difference between that and 2.000 to 4.000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't know on what basis, on the basis of which decision the army was going to take over military records?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I really didn't know, nor was I interested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these activists of the SDA were in the way of the army's efforts and prevented them from taking the records.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I wasn't on any side. I wasn't an activist of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any case, the army gave up and left without ever taking these records.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: What I heard was that some sort of agreement was reached with regard to that military documentation and that they -- these records were removed from the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It follows that on the 30th of August, 1991, the leadership of the SDA organised this protest in order to prevent the army from taking over the military records, and the Serbs were protesting because somebody was preventing the implementation of official decisions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: You should ask people who know. They should testify about this. All I know is that the army troops came to take over the military records and that the people were against it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is it true that as a result of that whole situation in Bratunac the presidents of the SDA and the SDS, that means both the Muslim and the Serb parties, issues a joint statement to calm the population down and promised that everything would be all right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Well, those joint statements were not rare. They issued that kind of thing very often. They made promises, issued guarantees trying to appease the people. They might have issued that one as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the same page, 3, paragraph 6, you talk about December 1991 when a convoy stopped a convoy including military trucks owned by the JNA towing artillery and you say at that point in time Serbs were arming themselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Well, you couldn't help arriving at that conclusion. Everybody in that situation would have thought the same thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you know, at that point did Muslims already have paramilitary formations? Were they already armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: What sort of arms are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what you say in your statement, but let's move on. You mention artillery. Was this artillery also distributed to the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I don't know. Do you think that this artillery was brought and given to the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It wasn't given to anyone. It was a convoy of the JNA passing through.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I really don't know, and I can't say anything. I cannot say that Bratunac had any military or paramilitary Muslim formations. Because I had Serb friends, I don't know -- I'm not sure, and I don't believe that anybody would give me any information about any sort of distribution of weapons. I don't know whether it was going on. At any rate, I was never Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. offered a rifle, ammunition, or anything of that kind. Whether paramilitary or military formations existed, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know nothing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I know nothing. I told you, I lived in a neighbourhood which was very evenly mixed and where there was not a single meeting about the distribution of weapons. It was impossible to hold anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know nothing about the arming of Muslim paramilitary formations in surrounding villages either?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: No. All I know is that when weapons were confiscated from these villages because by the 10th of May all the weapons had been seized and the population expelled, none of these weapons that were seized were automatic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that before the 10th of May the villagers there were armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: No. That's what you are saying. I can't give you the exact date. It might have been the 21st or the 23rd of May. I saw a poster with a proclamation outside of my house, signed by somebody named General Milosevic. It informed the people that a seizure of weapons was under way for Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the call-up of military conscripts towards the end of 1991 and the beginning of 1992 for military training in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: No one from Bratunac went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know nothing about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: No, because I had no links with those villages. I just went to work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But on page 4, you say that in the Crisis Staff formed by the SDS including Miroslav Deronjic, president of the SDS, Ljubisa Simic from the SDS leadership. There was also Dragisa Loncarevic and someone named Dragan referred to everyone as Kinez. And you know nothing about the establishment of the SDA, but you know about the activities of the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: That's not what I said. I said I knew who was the president of the SDA. I knew who the president of the municipality of Bratunac was. And I know this as well. I know the president of the municipality was this gentleman from --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it that you didn't say? I'm quoting from your statement. You say, "Members of the municipal Crisis Staff in 1992 were the following: Deronjic, Simic, Loncarevic, and this Dragan."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes, but you said that I stated somewhere that I was not familiar with the SDA structures in the municipality of Bratunac. I don't remember ever saying anything of the sort. I'm just talking in this particular paragraph about people from the SDS. As far as the SDA is concerned, I can tell you who was in their structures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm asking you is this: Can you tell us who the members were of the Crisis Staff of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I don't know that there was a Crisis Staff of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are claiming it didn't exist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I didn't say that. I don't know that it existed. I know the president of the party in the last days before the war was Dzevad Gusic. I know the president of the municipality was Nijaz Dubicic. I know that the deputy chief at the MUP was Senad Hodzic, and I can enumerate them as well as I enumerated the SDS people. Whether they had a Crisis Staff or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know nothing about clandestine Muslim paramilitary formations or their activities, and you claim that this attack on the column of cadets withdrawing from Rajlovac on the 14th of April is my invention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He has answered this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything, since you are talking about early 1992, do you know anything the meeting of the representatives of the SDA from Bratunac, Srebrenica, Zvornik, Vlasenica? That was early February 1992. That means long before the outbreak of the conflict. And the meeting discussed preparations for the war. That is another thing written in this book by Besim Ibisevic. You say you didn't read it. I'm just asking you whether you know about these events.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I don't remember that these meetings were held at all, because I didn't think that they were important. I didn't think SDS meetings were important either. Maybe these meetings were held in secret. Maybe ordinary people couldn't even know about it. Because as far as I can see, you get your information probably from people who attended these meetings and who were placed far above me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, since you know, that with increasing frequency there was a polarisation going on at the time. Do you know how it came about that separate police forces, Serb and Muslims -- Muslim were formed in town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Oh, you mean the division of the MUP in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what I mean. How did it happen? Was it decided at the meeting of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I don't know at which session this decision to divide the MUP was taken and on the basis of which document, but I know that all of a sudden two MUPs, two police forces, came into being in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do you know about their functioning, the two MUPs, one Serb, one Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I have no idea how they functioned. They probably didn't function at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you remember that under those circumstances when tensions were already high, do you remember, because you must have read newspapers and followed events, that the Presidency of the Bosnia and Herzegovina, without any representatives of the Serb population took the decision to mobilise the army, the police, the forces of the Civil Defence, all these structures being still within the federal system?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. All I know is that nobody mobilised me to either side. I don't know whether there were any Territorial Defence units mobilised in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how else could this 2nd Corps have been established, this force, whatever you call it, Green Berets, the patriotic people's league or whatever? How do you explain that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Well, probably the people on the other side were wiser. They didn't believe what we believed, and they had prepared for the war, and they didn't pay the price that we paid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Izetbegovic on the 12th of April ordered an all-out and unprovoked attack on all barracks of the JNA in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Well, Izetbegovic never informed me of anything, nor did he ask my advice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about a well-known event, about an order for attack. Do you know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that on the 6th of May, that means after those numerous local provocations and ambushes on local roads, a major armed attack was undertaken by Muslim formations on one of compact Serb populated areas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Which populated area?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A hamlet of Bljecevo village, populated by 532 Muslims and only 171 Serbs. That happened on the 6th of May, 1992, in a Muslim village. Their Muslim-organised forces killed 3 Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Thank you for reminding me that it was the 6th of May because I really couldn't remember the date. I know that a killing occurred, but what I know about is the killing of a family of one policeman from Bratunac, Branimir Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the 6th of May is an Orthodox religious holiday, Djurdjevdan, the patron saint's day for many Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I am aware of the holiday, but one thing is not clear about this murder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Please go on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I don't know who committed this killing. I would really have to be 100 per cent sure before pointing my finger at anyone. But I know that this policeman, Branislav or Branimir Jovanovic, remained on the side of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina after the division of the MUP, and I know from very reliable sources that Mr. Jovanovic worked for the state security of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And what is most surprising and curious to me, the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina had not yet started in many areas. And there was never any investigation of that murder. And even today, five or six years after the war, nobody ever took the trouble to investigate that murder, because as far as Brano Jovanovic is concerned, he was a remarkable man, and I don't see why Muslims should kill the family of a man who remained to serve the state security of Bosnia and Herzegovina. But I'm not claiming otherwise, either. But you should also know and emphasise that a mass attack was carried out later in Bljecevo. It was shelled from all sorts of artillery positions on the hills around Bratunac. So instead of conducting an investigation, they carried out an attack on Bljecevo village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the killing of those three Serbs.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I know about two. I don't know about the third one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the 27th of May in Konjevic Polje? Do you know that the Muslim extremists set up an ambush there which intercepted a column of freight vehicles, heavy-duty vehicles returning from Zvornik? And they were carrying bauxite ore and that five drivers who were Serbs were skilled on that particular occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: The period round about the 27th of May, is that what you said? Well, unfortunately, I wasn't able to take account of my own family let alone the columns and alleged attacks and the destruction of those columns. On the 27th of May, in fact, I was in Visoko and was recuperating from some of the injuries that I had received -- that I had received, and my psychological traumas, from my days in the Bratunac camp and at Pale. So everything that happened after the 10th of May, because that was when I was shut up in the camp, incarcerated there, I cannot know anything about events subsequent to that, nor can I say anything about them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Milosevic, your time is up. You've had two minutes over, but you can ask a final question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, all right, Mr. May. Then I'll have to skip over many of the questions I have here. I have the lists of Serbs who were killed in all these villages. So there's no point in going into that now. And there's no point in me asking for additional time. That is quite clear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic. Mr. Milosevic, you said you wanted to ask some questions about Serbs being killed. To what point, to what end, may I ask? What would you be seeking to show from that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the last question. Well, what I want to say is that I want to ask the witness whether he knows about the fact that throughout that territory, this broad territory around Bratunac Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and Srebrenica, covering about 1.000 square kilometres in all, that the Serbs were pushed into just 25 to 30 square kilometres and that all the Serbian villages except two in the area of Bratunac were razed to the ground and the population killed. That is the say the inhabitants who had not managed to flee to Bratunac or across the Drina River into Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Before you answer, let us have it clarified. When is it suggested that this happened so the witness can answer it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything happened in 1992 and 1993, Mr. May. And, for example, I can tell you that for the Orthodox Christmas, the Orthodox Christmas therefore, that is to say in January 1993, once again one of the most bloody crimes were committed precisely in that area, and the religious Orthodox holidays are quite customarily used for crimes to be perpetrated again the Serbs living in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I take it this was after the 17th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can't ask him anything about what actually happened in Bratunac because you say that after that, he has nothing to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as you learnt about these events from various people but not from those who had taken part in the events themselves, you yourself state that on the 10th of May, you were expelled from your house under threat of arms; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: On the 10th of May, not only I myself was expelled from my home but so were all those who were in the hamlets or various districts around my area and Bratunac too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me who expelled you from your homes on -- at gunpoint and all the rest of them on the 10th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I was expelled by the paramilitary formations, the Territorial Defence of Bratunac municipality as well as the Yugoslav People's Army who attended all these goings-on with their APCs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I don't suppose you want to say that the JNA soldiers expelled you from your houses. Did they?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's not said that. He has said that it was people who said they were from the Belgrade MUP. But you now have had an extra few minutes. Yes, Mr. Kay. Questioned by Mr. Kay:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you've made two statements, the first dated the 29th of June, 1992, which was given to the Ministry of Interior for the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told to put anything into that statement that was not true or was not of your own knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: In the statement, I state quite exactly the events that I saw myself, and I also speak about events that I heard about. But nobody told me what I should state or not state in the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You gave a second statement dated the 10th of October, 1998 to the Prosecutors of the Tribunal. Were you told to put anything into that statement that wasn't true or wasn't what you knew about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: No. Nobody advised me as to what I was to state.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're going to look at both of those statements now, so if the Judges would have both statements, and I'm be obviously using the English language version, before them. And if the witness could have both statements in his own language before him. In your evidence today, you said that there were only two paramilitary units in Bratunac, and you said that that was the Eagles and Arkan's men. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we just look at your statement of the 29th of June, 1992, paragraph 1, you mention in that statement and for a number of pages thereafter that in Bratunac, on the 17th of April, 1992, were Seselj's men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any deference between Seselj's men and the Eagles and Arkan's men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Between the White Eagles and Seselj's men there is no difference. But between Arkan's men and Seselj's men, yes, there is an enormous difference. They were different commanders commanding the men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In both those statements, you identify various local people who were working with Seselj's men. Is that because you knew those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement of the 29th of June, 1992, you don't mention Arkan's men being present until the 10th of May of 1992. Paragraph 17 of that statement in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Page 7 at the top in the original B/C/S version with Registry number 2875 in the top right-hand corner, 2875.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what is the position? What did Arkan's men, do you say, enter Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Arkan's men and Seselj's men, well, perhaps I didn't say. I didn't give the title of the units, but Arkan's men and Seselj's men, when I say that I meant the paramilitary formations who were present in Bratunac as of the 17th of April. Up until about the 20th of May when they withdrew from Bratunac and then again from the 20 something of April until the 10th of May when I was deported from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you describe the local people being involved with Seselj's men, the Eagles, were they working with them as a joint group, force together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Likewise with Arkan's men, when you mention the local people were they working with them as a joint group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Actions within the cleansing of villages around Bratunac were perpetrated by the paramilitary formations and the Territorial Defence which was there in a regular fashion, mobilised in the regular way and set up. The army of the Serbs was set up in that way. I assume that that's what they would be called. But both Seselj's men and Arkan's men took part in the operations together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement of the 10th of October, 1998, and I'm looking at page 4, paragraph 19, you mention the Serbian paramilitary forces being replaced by the regular JNA army. And in paragraph 20, you mention the Drina Corps. That is in your statement to the Tribunal investigators; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Could you give me the page, please, where that is?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can take it from me that it is right, that I'm not misrepresenting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: He's entitled to see it. On page bottom right-hand corner number 4 of the second statement Registry number at the top right-hand corner will be either 889 or 868.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I be of assistance to the witness. It is page 4, the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement of the 29th of June 1992, and we will look at page 2, paragraphs 3 and 4, you mention there the Semberija Corps consisting of military reservists, and you mention in paragraph 4 the TO and the TO flag being put on a building. Now, when you refer to the TO, do you refer to the JNA? What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I mean the local Serb formations which were mobilised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the local army and not the regular JNA would be right to describe any military activity that you saw; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: No. No. You asked me, sir, what I meant when I say -- said Territorial Defence, and I said that Territorial Defence to me implies the local inhabitants. I did not say that the army did not take part or the army of Yugoslavia was not there. It was there together and took part with the Territorial Defence, the paramilitary formations, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why in your statement then of the 29th of June, 1992, did you not mention the regular JNA? Why is it to the investigators of the Tribunal is it that you mention the regular JNA? Why is there a difference between the two statements describing which forces were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: In the statement of 1992 as well, I mentioned the Yugoslav People's Army, because to my mind, I think that -- I think they misunderstood me or you misunderstood me. When I say regular JNA, I meant the forces that came from outside, and that was the so-called Semberija Corps, whereas when I say Territorial Defence, I meant the local Serbs who were mobilised from the municipality of Bratunac. So it's quite correct. I know that for the Semberija Corps, I considered them to be forces of the Yugoslav People's Army because they weren't locals from the area. I never came across regular -- actually, when I say "regular soldiers," they were children up to the ages of 18 or 20 who were doing their military service. And the forces who were here were those which had been mobilised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to deal now with the part of your evidence where you said that you were arrested by police from Belgrade, and in your statement on the 29th of June, 1992, that's paragraph 12. And in your statement on the 10th of October, 1998, that's paragraph 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think it appropriate that the witness should have a chance to look at these paragraphs in detail. Paragraph 12 of the first statement by my calculation, it's a little bit -- to be quite precise starts at the foot of page 4 of the B/C/S of the first statement, four lines up from the bottom, and the -- the witness might like to have a look at that and have a chance to consider the points being made by Mr. Kay. Paragraph 25 of the second statement can be found I think on the bottom right-hand corner, page 5 of it. I'd ask that the witness be satisfied that he's got them before him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kay. What is the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I hope the witness has got the paragraphs now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we look at the paragraph 12 of the 29th of June, 1992, it says that the event there of your arrest happened on the 26th of April, 1992, but in the statement of the 10th of October, 1998, it says it's the 30th of April. Can you explain the different dates in two different statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: The statement given to the investigators of The Hague Tribunal was given seven or eight years later after the first statement that was given straight away after I arrived in the Tuzla canton. During my testimony here today, I drew attention to the fact that I might be mistaken when quoting dates, or I might forget a name, for example. But I can never forget the actual event. And it is quite true that I was arrested on the 26th of April, taken away from my house by people who introduced themselves as being members of the police from Belgrade, the MUP of Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as far as you're concerned, we should take the date 26th -- 29th of June, 1992, as being the more accurate statement; is that right? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. I think that's a very generalised comment. The witness can't deal with that. We've heard his evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that statement of the 29th of June, you say that, "The police surrounded my house," and in the statement of the 10th of October, you say you were arrested at a neighbour's house. Is there any difference between the two, and if so, why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Please, let me just find that portion where I say that I was arrested in a neighbour's house. In both statements, I say quite specifically that I was sitting in my neighbour's yard, and my neighbours were Jamb. And I saw three or four cars come to my house, surround my house. And as I was -- the house I was in is just 10 metres away from my own house. I went into my own yard and surrendered myself to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the statement of the 29th of June you say that two bullets were fired so, "It looked as though I had been killed." But in the statement of the 10th of October, you say that the two shots were fired and, "They told me that they had killed my wife and children." Can you explain the difference there is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: After I got into the car, one of the cars, one car followed, the car I was in, and in front of my house you could hear several gunshots. And in the car, when I was in the car, they told me that they had killed my family and that it was my turn next. Now, at that same time, from the car I was in a man fired two shots, and they told my family that I had been killed and that when they leave they can come and pick up my body. And that was one of the most terrible moments I have ever experienced in my whole life, because for several hours I was convinced that my whole family, my parents, my sister, my mother, and so on, were all killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're saying four shots were fired rather than two; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: No. I didn't say that either two or four shots were fired. I said that several shots could be heard from my house, and from the car I was in, two shots were fired. And they explained to my family that I had been killed, and the other shots that were fired, they said to me that my family had been killed, including my wife and children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement of the 10th of October, 1998, it's the next paragraph, at paragraph 26, you say after your release that you stayed at home for the next ten days all the time. In your statement of the 29th of June, 1992, if we go to page 7, paragraphs 13 to 17, there is a large number of events and details of events happening in the Bratunac area between the 30th of April and the 10th of May.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Part of the unit of the Territorial Defence or, rather, part of the unit which was specially set up in the Bratunac municipality for purposes of that kind was called the Diversionary Reconnaissance Unit and many of my neighbours were members of that unit. And every day I saw them go into action, go off into operation. And I always trembled, wondering whether they would come back at all, whether they might be killed or wounded perhaps. So we were all afraid for them. And I heard many things from them too, because very often we would be sitting around drinking together, and they would open up and tell us things, and I learnt some things later on when I was exchanged and when I was with those people. And they were from all over the Bratunac municipality, and they were in the camp together with me. So I learnt of the details. So in no statement did I see that people in Glogova was burnt and people killed or any other villages. And I stress everywhere in my statements that I heard that this had happened, not that I had seen it happen myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Some matters arising. Re-examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we please just clarify your own observations of incoming forces from Serbia? You've already spoken of the event where earlier on in September you saw artillery going for the small -- going towards the small Serb villages close to Bratunac. What kind of force was that artillery? Because it JNA? Was it Territorial Defence? What was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: That convoy made up of seven trucks which left in the direction of Kravica belonged to the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've been asked about who was provided with those weapons. Was there any Muslim person in that small village to be provided with weapons or were those villages all Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Kravica is a large local community which comprises about ten completely ethnically pure Serb villages. So in all of those villages, not a single one belonging to the Kravica local community were there any Muslim inhabitants. They were purely Serb villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning now, then, to the takeover of Bratunac itself. You've spoken of the role of the two paramilitary groups that you identified to help Mr. Kay. When in addition to those troops were you first aware of any regular army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I became aware of that on the 17th of April. That was the first time I saw the regular Yugoslav army that was at the meeting in Fontana, the Fontana Hotel. I saw four guards in full military dress standing in front of the hotel, and I suppose there were some officers there attending the negotiations. On the second occasion, the Yugoslav army, Yugoslav soldiers, appeared sometime after the 20th of April. Yes, the 20th of April, after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were challenged on this. Mr. Kay says you used the Semberija Corps on one occasion and Drina Corps on another. Can you help us with your knowledge of the difference between those two and explain why one statement may say one thing and one another?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I did not mention anywhere that the Drina Corps was present in Bratunac. As far as I remember, did -- I did say that the information which was to the effect that the Muslims should surrender their arms was signed by the commander of the 2nd -- the Drina Corps, the commander of the Drina Corps. I did not say in actual fact that the Drina Corps was present in Bratunac at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's to be found on paragraph 20 of the witness's later statement, page 4, and indeed accords with what's there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've been challenged about or asked questions about your arrest, your first arrest and the use of gunshot to frighten you and/or your family. If in the first statement you didn't mention the use made of the guns to that effect, any reason for it when you made that first statement? Was this matter particularly important to you or not or can't you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I'm quite certain that when I gave both my statements to the people who took down those statements, I did mention those gunshots. However, why in one statement there is something which is not in the other statement, I really can't say. However, I'm quite sure that the shots could be heard, were heard, and I spent one, two, perhaps three hours in -- totally upset, thinking that my family had really been killed, and I don't see why I should mention this in one and not the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sticking with the point that's been raised about incoming Serb personnel, to use a neutral term, those special police who interrogated you on that first occasion, what if anything did any of them say that explained that he was from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: When I was brought into a hall, I was left to wait there for about half an hour until that so-called inspector arrived from the Belgrade MUP, who introduced himself as being an inspector of the Belgrade MUP. And he was the person who asked me the questions. And the guards too, because when I was -- during the time I spent in those premises, the inspector would go out of the room and come back several times. So that the guard told me --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, very well. Carry on then. I think that's -- very well. The guard told you what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: The guard told me that the man was indeed a member of the Belgrade MUP. I don't know why they introduced themselves that way, why they told me that, but that's what they did tell me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've been asked by Mr. Kay about the following period when you say you were at home and as your first statement reveals, accounting -- giving an account of what you heard. And as your second statement reveals, summarising it, I think, an account that would suggest up to some 200 people were killed in those early days before you were ever shepherded off to the stadium and the gymnasium. At that stage when you were at home but you were hearing of people being killed, where to your knowledge was the regular JNA unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: The killing began after the arrival of those, let's call them special forces from the Belgrade MUP and after the return of Arkan's men or, rather, Seselj's men, the paramilitaries. Whereas the forces of the Yugoslav People's Army were stationed in Bratunac with their own military vehicles, and they were behind the Fontana Hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can see the Fontana Hotel in tab 4. Was anything said to you by your comrades -- it can come onto the -- we can just put it on the overhead projector if necessary to make sure you can see it. There. Mine's available if that will save time. Was anything said to you by those giving an account of the killings being done in the town of Bratunac about the JNA unit that was behind the Fontana Hotel intervening with the killings or trying to stop people doing what they were doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: My house is about 4 to 500 metres away from the centre of Bratunac. So if I wasn't moving around there, my friends and neighbours were. So the flow of information was so good that at each point in time somebody would learn that one of the inhabitants of Bratunac were taken off, never to return. The units of the Yugoslav People's Army or shall we call -- at least those units that I considered to belong to the Yugoslav People's Army units from their entry into town never intervened to protect any of the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were then compelled with your family to leave your house, unlocked for the purposes for looting, as we know, and to be taken to the stadium, thence to the gymnasium of the school, what part did the JNA army unit take in that process?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I only know that the JNA assisted in the cleansing of Muslim villages with their armoured vehicles. They accompanied the units that were cleansing the villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Back to the question. When you were actually taken to the stadium, and let's deal with it in this way: When you were in the stadium and the men of army -- yes, army age were separated from women, children, and the elderly, was the JNA unit there? If so, what part did it take in that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: There were tanks around the stadium, as well as APCs. They were providing security for the stadium. So they were present. They secured the stadium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you marched --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do you want the usher to remain?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The second question is the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No. But in light of the questions I must deal with these matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were taken to the gymnasium, why the JNA units involved in that, shepherding, your being moved -- your move to the gymnasium?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: No. We were shepherded by paramilitary units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were in the gymnasium and by your account 6 or 700 people were killed, you've told us what you could hear. You tell us in your statement what you could hear by way of shooting at night or in the daytime. How near or far was the school from where the JNA was based even assuming it wasn't on the streets as it had been when you were taken to the stadium? How far away was the Fontana Hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: About 200 metres. Two hundred to 300 metres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us about one aspect of the removal of bodies, a lorry carrying the bodies. To your knowledge, was it just one lorry or one occasion or was it several lorries on many occasions or don't you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: In front of the hangar and the hall, one could hear trucks coming and going all the time. Groups of people were taken out of the gym -- gymnasium who were constantly loading the bodies. So there were several lorries.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm actually going to be a few more minutes, I'm afraid, with this. But I'm entirely in the Court's hands. I can deal with it now or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: A few more minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it's been said that you don't know where those mass graves that must have been built to take those bodies were, but nevertheless, it was several lorries moving in and out of the school. Do you know which road they took?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: It is not correct that I don't know, because quite recently, I think towards the end of last year, one of the mass graves was found in the area of the Redzici village, and it is assumed that it contains men from the hall who were killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As to that mass grave, just help us. Would the route to it pass by the Fontana Hotel where, if they weren't on the streets, the JNA unit would have been based or would it be in another direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: No, I really don't know --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: -- where they drove off those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally on the topic of the JNA's presence, when you were eventually moved for exchange to Pale, what were the forces that moved you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: We were taken there by the newly formed police, and we were escorted, I think, by two APCs of the Yugoslav People's Army or whichever army it was that was present at that time in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as your statement makes clear, you were disguised on the basis that you might be thought to be people arrested for crimes with a second truck carrying the weapons, it was being suggested, for those looking, had been taken off you; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I didn't say that I was disguised. I never said in any statement that I was disguised or masked or that we prisoners were masked. It seems to me, and I'm quite sure that what I said was that after we were prepared for an exchange, leaving the hall at Pale, a corridor was formed of Serbs who were masked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: And who --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Forgive me. My mistake in the question I asked in order to save time. In the move to Pale, was there another lorry sent containing weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: After the exchange, I learnt that the mass media in Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina, which was at the time under the authority of the Bosnian Serbs, that they announced that we were a group of Ustashas captured in the fighting around Srebrenica and that with them personal weapons had been brought with us, that that had been confiscated from us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as you've already explained, this movement was accompanied by the movement of the two APCs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a couple more questions. I can delete the remainder although they might have been useful, but I'll try and delete them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To give -- you were asked a question by Mr. Kay about, I think, about the locals being compelled to work with the incoming forces. Help us with this if you can: Just yes or no, was there a time when you were able to return to Bratunac after the conflict and at least speak to people who were living there then? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find yourself and were you prepared to speak to those who you recognised as having been involved in these atrocities on the Serb side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: I didn't talk to people that I was sure had committed atrocities, but I did talk to people who were, for instance, were in the escort when I was being held, who were guarding me at the stadium. One of my friends, in fact, had taken some money from me and thrown it onto a pile that was designated for that purpose. So did I spoke to those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Explain to the Judges if you would be so good, please, why it was you were prepared to speak to people who had been involved at any event to that extent when you saw them after these events? What did they explain to you about what it was that they'd been doing and why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Out of all the Serbs in Bratunac, my personal opinion is that maybe some 10 per cent only enjoyed what was going on. Ten per cent or so were against what was happening, and 80 per cent of them were passive observers who simply feared for their families. Many of them explained to me later on that they had to do what they did because they feared what would happen to their families, and I believe them. Why wouldn't I believe them? And I forgive them for what --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, the accused on several occasions pressed you for opinions on what led to all this and ultimately suggested to you that it was all fanned by the flames of the secession of Bosnia-Herzegovina. He didn't use the word nationalism there, but that was the theme of many of his questions. If you feel you can -- I say finally there is a document I must put in. If you feel you can, having been asked that questioned so many times, comment on your understanding as a resident of the cause of this conflict, can you do so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Unfortunately, my opinion differs from the opinion of many on both sides. For a long time after everything that happened to me, for years and years, I spent many nights thinking what it was that resulted in thousands of innocent people laying down their lives for nothing. The creation of a new state doesn't mean that anyone can put it in his pocket and take it to another continent. We continued to be neighbours, continued to live next to one another. Nobody prevented anyone from taking any power. 80 per cent of the power in Bratunac was held by Serbs, they headed all public institutions, and nobody thought that this was a bad thing. My personal opinion is that nationalism was not the spark that triggered those events. I think, after all, that it was crime that predominated or, rather, that nationalism was just used to cover up what was to take place later. It would have been much easier for me to understand that -- that Serbia had become a powerful country, a country of prosperity, a country in which citizens are leading a normal life after they embarked upon that war to create a greater Serbia. But all that has been created is a beast that is swallowing up its own people. So I believe what happened on one side and the other and a third was prompted by crimes and criminals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You know, Mr. Nice, we've spent more than 20 minutes on this re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And it's a question of whether it's really necessary in a witness like this. But let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... And go I may say so, Your Honour, when the accused asks, and always in a tendentious way, for opinions there can be occasions when opinions of witnesses on the ground can be extremely valuable I respectfully suggest. My last question relates to the accused's suggestion that this witness was in a position to be committing crimes in certain months of 1992 and he's spoken of the document he's producing. It can now become an exhibit with your leave, perhaps it can be become Tab 6.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Tab 5, Prosecutor's Exhibit 440.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you just look at this. It will have to be under seal, it can't be revealed, of course. Is this the document showing your joining up the army in March of 1993? And that's as much detail as I'll give.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1070
utterances.text: Your Honours, I could have provided a certificate from the local community, the municipality in which I was, and everyone would have suspected that that certificate was given without any grounds. I have produced a valid document which confirms and indicates exactly where I was on a particular date, of which unit I was a member, and on what location I was to be found on a particular date. So there's no chance is that I could have been anywhere else except in these places which are indicated and stamped in this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The statement is what happened to him in the meantime in hospital. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Witness B-1070, thank you for attending and coming to the court to give your evidence. It's now concluded and you're free to go. Mr. Milosevic, we'll hear your point when we come back. We're going to adjourn now. Twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you had a point when we went out, and I had said we would hear you. Maybe the moment has passed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to object, Mr. May, because the witness who testified a moment ago was this morning transformed from a viva voce witness to a 92 bis witness. His examination-in-chief was reduced to a minimum, and this of course affected my own cross-examination. And after that, you gave Mr. Nice all of half an hour for so-called re-examination, which did not relate to any new facts, and I think it was not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I will deal with that. In fact, it was 20 minutes. You heard me make some comment as to the length. But so you understand the rules, the Prosecution do have a right to re-examine a witness after cross-examination, and that does include these 92 bis witnesses. And in a sense, it can be said to be a right which is more important with them because the Prosecution has not had time or the usual time with them beforehand. So there is a right to re-examine. You will have it in due course when you call your evidence. But it's obviously one which should be exercised fairly circumspectly and not taking at too great a length. Yes. We will have the next witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the next witness is B-1237. There are two preliminary matters I would like to raise with the Court prior to him being called. The first is, Your Honour, I became aware of earlier today of a technical breach of Rule 90(C) and that is the prohibition of one witness seeing the testimony of another. This particular witness had asked to see the courtroom, and he was brought by a member of the OTP staff into the public gallery for approximately two minutes. He was there. Apparently the proceedings were broadcast in his language. The witness who was testifying at that time was Mr. Gusic, a witness from a different municipality, and he was testifying or he was being cross-examined at the time about removal of arms from the Territorial Defence of that -- of Bratunac municipality. Nothing that this witness will testify about. I believe it's merely a technical violation. I have advised or sent out notice to the members of the team reminding them of our obligations under 90(C), but I did want to bring it to the Chamber's attention that such did occur.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the second matter, Your Honour, is this witness is a protected witness. The Prosecution will be seeking to take some of his testimony in closed session. If I might summarise his presence at four meetings. Some of those meetings he will discuss and is requesting that simply the participants in the meeting be taken in closed session. One of the meetings and it is of substantial length and probably the most significant thing he will testify about is a meeting in which -- that is so notorious with so few participants that he feels there is no way he can Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. refer to that meeting in open session without clearly identifying himself or the limited number of other participants and fears not only for his safety but their safety as well. And finally the last portion that we would seek to take in closed session and very briefly is a map where he's identified the precise locations where he was at particular times. He fears taking this in open session would identify him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We will have the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you'd like to take a seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that we begin the testimony of this witness -- I realise I'm causing the usher having to run, but to show the witness tab 1 of a binder of exhibits we would wish to use with this witness, I'd ask the binder be assigned a number at this juncture.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, Prosecutor's Exhibit 441. Examined by Mr. Groome:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question to you is I'd ask you to look at the top of Prosecution Exhibit 441, tab 1. Is that your name at the top of the page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1237
utterances.text: Yes, at the top of the page is my full first and last name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the purposes of protecting your identity, I will refer you as B-1237. Have you seen the remainder of this page in preparation for your testimony here today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1237
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen the rest of this page. All the data on it are correct, and today I did not prepare myself for the testimony at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you willing to answer additional questions about your educational and professional background?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1237
utterances.text: I am ready to answer all questions which will assist for the truth to be proven.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm finished with that exhibit. Thank you, usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I want to begin your testimony by asking you some basic background questions regarding Zvornik. Can you tell us approximately how many people were living in Zvornik prior to the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1237
utterances.text: Prior to the conflict there were about 80.000 people living in Zvornik municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. The remainder of today's hearing is going to be in fact in closed session. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
